your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Accepting this hands p3 a monopoly they can build on today. Charging a lot of cash keeps them from building fast and pays for my push toward NC and the greens. I'll take anything around $300 or more.
Kentucky completes my reds, and I still have ~$870 to build. p1 is cash-starved. I could go up to ~$350.
Ceiling is about $450. Paying $800 leaves no building cash. p1 is desperate, so hold firm.

$800 would wipe out my building cash and pay for p1's houses. I'm raising to $425 plus the GOOJF card. My hard ceiling is around $500 in total value. If p1 refuses, I'll hold and look for other trades.

Without a monopoly I lose to pink, orange and yellow, so I need red. At $700 I'd still afford about 2 houses on each red after unmortgaging and mortgaging the others, but money that big also turns p1's orange into a monster. Aim for $550-600. I'd likely accept up to $625 plus the card.

This is within my ceiling of about $625 plus the card. It completes reds. After the trade I'll have $522. Unmortgage Kentucky for $121. Mortgage the non-set lots (PRR, Pacific, Penn Ave, Boardwalk) if needed to get to 3 houses per red quickly. Watch out for p1's orange, since they now have cash.
Unmortgaging for $121 leaves me $390. Next, mortgage the non-set lots (PRR, Pacific, Penn, Boardwalk) to fund houses on the reds. Aim for 3 houses each if I can, since that's where rent jumps.
Plan: mortgage Pacific, Penn Ave, PRR, and maybe Boardwalk (~$999 total), then build 2 houses on each red. The squares ahead are mostly mine or harmless, so it's safe to run low on cash.

Mortgaging Penn Ave brings me to $689. Next, mortgage PRR to reach $789, then build about 4 houses and keep roughly $190 as a buffer against p1's orange and p4's utilities. Boardwalk stays unmortgaged for now.
PRR earns little. Mortgage it for $100, which brings me to $349. Then build a 2nd house on Illinois and keep about $199 as a buffer against p4's utilities and yellows.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $2364 and am on Oriental Avenue. I hold a full Brown monopoly with one house on Baltic, three Pinks with four houses each, and three Oranges with four houses each. My Greens are unimproved and unmortgaged. Park Place is mortgaged without Boardwalk.

All my railroads, utilities, and light blues are mortgaged. Player two has only $110 cash and all properties mortgaged. Players three and four are bankrupt. The bank now has seven houses and twelve hotels remaining.

Player two owns all three red properties but they are mortgaged, so they cannot build on them. They would need to unmortgage every property before they could improve anything.

Player two cannot unmortgage any red properties. The total cost is $374, but they only have $110. They are effectively deadlocked and cannot build anything. I am now deciding what to do on Oriental Avenue.

I am considering building hotels on my Pinks and Oranges. The bank has twelve hotels remaining, but each hotel costs four houses to build.

I am calculating the exact cost of building hotels. Each hotel costs four houses, and I am checking whether the rent from a hotel would exceed the rent from four houses on each property.

Upgrading all six properties to hotels would cost $600 and return 24 houses to the bank. Player two is on New York Avenue after paying $800 rent, so they will eventually pass GO and collect $200. That cash could let them unmortgage their red properties later. My goal is to bankrupt player two.

Player two cannot pay the $750 rent on St. Charles or States even after collecting $200 from passing GO. Hotels would not bankrupt them either, since their cash is too low to cover any pink or orange rent.

I will keep my houses locked. Player two has no houses to sell and cannot build anything right now, so returning them would not help them immediately. If they somehow raise enough cash later, they could unmortgage their red properties and start building again.

I will not trade with player two. I will not give them cash or unmortgage their properties. Unmortgaging my own holdings is unnecessary because they are already bankrupt.

Unmortgaging my light blues would cost $176 and is unnecessary. I have no railroads to unmortgage, and Park Place would cost about $193.

I will end my turn. I will not build hotels or trade.

I considered buying player two's red properties or Boardwalk to prevent any comeback. Unmortgaging Park Place and Boardwalk would let me build hotels on the dark blue monopoly. That would be devastating, but they are already bankrupt from my orange and pink holdings.

I rejected trading cash for player two's red properties. That would give them money they could use to survive another rent hit.

I also considered offering worthless mortgaged railroads or utilities in exchange for their reds. That would strip their only remaining monopoly, but they likely know those reds are their last chance.

I am weighing whether to build the last house on Mediterranean Avenue to match Baltic's single house. That would cost $50 and leave six houses in the bank, but player two cannot build anything so it is marginal.

I also considered upgrading the Brown properties to four houses each. That would consume more houses and raise rent, though player two likely cannot afford the higher rent on Baltic even with one house.
